items.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000
items.q: Well you interviewed Sol Yaged. ... Sol was there.

ctx.x: That’s amazing. How did they pay the musicians?

You’d go in and buy a beer. I’m not sure. They had a second story. They may have had an entrance fee because they put the bands up there. It may have cost you fifty cents or a dollar to get in. But you’d go there, and I’d just sit there and drink three or four bottles of beer in the night. Terrific. Marvelous. And as I say you stay at the bar and then as these people came off they’d swing by the bar and say hello and so on and so forth. And I’m trying to think — Cozy Cole. Cozy was there. And just everybody who…

items.title: Sol Yaged interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000

ctx.x: Well when they came up there, do they come up there with a band or you picked up a local band?
Usually, the fellow that I mentioned, Milt Fillius—
Right. Who knew me from the 40s.
